discovery: Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated electron systems

nominees.name: Antoine Georges
nominees.affiliation: Collège de France, Paris; Flatiron Institute, New York; University of Geneva

motivation: Vollhardt (with Metzner) showed that lattice models of interacting electrons become exactly tractable in the limit of infinite dimensions, where the self-energy becomes local. Georges and Kotliar then turned this insight into dynamical mean-field theory: an exact mapping of the lattice problem onto a quantum impurity in a self-consistent bath. DMFT gave the first unified, nonperturbative description of the Mott metal-insulator transition, capturing both the coherent quasiparticles and the Hubbard bands, along with their transfer of spectral weight. Combined with electronic-structure methods, it became the standard quantitative tool for correlated materials: transition-metal oxides, actinides, iron pnictides, nickelates, and the Hund's metal concept. Its predictions have been confirmed by photoemission, optics and transport. Few theoretical ideas have changed so deeply how physicists calculate and understand the quantum many-electron problem in real materials.
